claims.text: As of 28 July 2026, a total of 109 deaths and 360 injuries have been reported nationwide. The majority of casualties resulted from house collapses and flash floods triggered by heavy rainfall. Additionally, 796 houses have been damaged, either fully or partially, while 379 livestock have perished.

Re-checked 11 August 2026: reliefweb.int again returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch. A targeted web search found no OCHA 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' or any other allowlisted report newer than Situation Update - 1 (3 August 2026); non-allowlisted Pakistani press (Pakistan Today, Daily Times) continues to cite NDMA for a toll around 151 deaths as of 8 August 2026, still not corroborated on an allowlisted source. The cited figures (126 deaths, 416 injuries nationwide) remain unchanged.

OCHA, 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' (as of 10 August 2026, infographic sourced to NDMA's Monsoon situation report covering 26 June-9 August 2026, plus PMD and WFP data): 'Deaths: 153,' 'Injured: 457,' 'Houses Damaged: 1,339 total (432 Fully Damaged and 907 Partially Damaged),' 'Livestock Lost: 576.'

NDMA, Monsoon 2026 Daily Situation Report No. 47 (11 August 2026): cumulative casualties and injuries table, 'From 26 June 2026 to 11 August 2026' -- Grand Total Deceased 155 (52 male, 30 female, 73 children), Grand Total Injured 460 (195 male, 113 female, 152 children). Cumulative damage table for the same period: Houses Full 432, Partial 909, Total 1,341; Livestock Perished 580. The last-24-hours entry for 11 August records 1 injury (Narowal, Punjab), no new deaths, and 1 partial house damaged.

NDMA Monsoon 2026 Daily Situation Report No. 49 (covering 1300 hrs 12 August - 1300 hrs 13 August 2026): cumulative deaths unchanged at 155 (52 male, 30 female, 73 children); injured risen to 468 (up from 460, +8 in the last 24 hours, all in Rajanpur, Punjab); houses damaged (cumulative) risen to 1,345 (432 fully damaged, 913 partially damaged, up from 1,341); livestock perished unchanged at 580; cumulative rescue operations since 26 June 2026: 1,111 operations, 8,700 persons rescued.

Re-checked 14 August 2026: NDMA's Monsoon 2026 sitrep archive shows Daily Situation Report No. 49 (13 August 2026) as still the latest published edition — no No. 50 has been posted; ReliefWeb's Pakistan country page and a search for 'Monsoon Situation Update - 3' returned nothing newer. Figures (155 deaths, 468 injured) remain unchanged.

NDMA and PDMA Punjab have moved from advisory to an active flood alert for the Chenab, Jhelum and Ravi rivers from 29 July-05 August, with evacuations already being directed in low-lying and riverbank areas.

Re-checked 1 August 2026: the Islamic Relief Pakistan humanitarian situation report (period 26 June-28 July 2026) remains the latest report in the 'PAK: Pluvial/Flash Flood - 06-2026' ReliefWeb update series; no newer edition has been published, and the 109 deaths/360 injuries figure is unchanged.

Re-checked 2 August 2026: no ReliefWeb report newer than the Islamic Relief Pakistan situation report (period 26 June-28 July 2026) has been found; figures remain unchanged, and NDMA/PDMA's active flood alert for the Chenab, Jhelum and Ravi rivers (29 July-5 August) remains in its stated window.

OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 1' infographic (as of 03 Aug 2026, posted to ReliefWeb 3 August 2026) states: 'Based on NDMA Monsoon situation report covering from 26 June to 2 August 2026, monsoon-related incidents have resulted in 126 deaths and 416 injuries across Pakistan... In addition, 1,119 houses have been damaged (352 fully damaged and 767 partially damaged), while 508 livestock have perished due to the monsoon-related hazards. The most affected areas in terms of housing damage include Gilgit-Baltistan, Balochistan, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, and AJ&K.'

Re-confirmed by direct fetch on 6 August 2026: OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 1' (as of 3 August 2026) remains the latest in its series; no 'Update - 2' has been published. Confirmed unchanged figures: '126 Deaths, 416 Injured, 1,119 Houses Damaged (352 Fully Damaged, 767 Partially Damaged), 508 Livestock Lost,' sourced to NDMA's Monsoon situation report covering 26 June-2 August 2026.

Re-checked 7 August 2026 via direct fetch of reliefweb.int/country/pak: OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 1' (as of 3 August 2026) remains the only entry in that series; no Situation Update - 2 has been published, and the on-file figures (126 deaths, 416 injured nationwide) are unchanged.

Re-checked 8 August 2026: no newer ReliefWeb/OCHA edition beyond the report already cited was found via search (reliefweb.int itself returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch today); non-allowlisted Pakistani press citing NDMA report a higher toll (151 deaths, 448 injured as of 8 August) that has not yet appeared on an allowlisted source, so the cited figures remain unchanged pending a citable update.

Re-checked 9 August 2026: ReliefWeb's Pakistan country page shows no OCHA 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update' edition newer than Situation Update - 1 (3 August 2026); the cited figures (126 deaths, 416 injuries nationwide) remain unchanged.

description: Heavy monsoon rains beginning around 26 June 2026 have triggered flash floods, riverine flooding and house collapses across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Punjab, Gilgit-Baltistan, Azad Jammu & Kashmir, Balochistan and Sindh. OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 1' infographic (as of 3 August 2026, posted to ReliefWeb 3 August 2026), based on NDMA's Monsoon situation report covering 26 June-2 August 2026, records 126 deaths and 416 injuries nationwide, mainly from house collapse, lightning strikes, flash floods, drowning, electrocution, tree falls, boulder falls, heavy rainfall and solar-panel-related incidents, along with 1,119 houses damaged (352 fully damaged, 767 partially damaged) and 508 livestock lost. The most affected areas for housing damage are Gilgit-Baltistan, Balochistan, Punjab, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and AJ&K. Pakistan's National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) and Punjab's Provincial Disaster Management Authority (PDMA) had earlier moved from an advisory to an active flood alert for the Chenab, Jhelum and Ravi rivers running 29 July-5 August 2026, with evacuations directed in low-lying and riverbank areas as monsoon rains continued. Re-checked 8 August 2026: no newer ReliefWeb/OCHA edition beyond the report already cited was found via search (reliefweb.int itself returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch today); non-allowlisted Pakistani press citing NDMA report a higher toll (151 deaths, 448 injured as of 8 August) that has not yet appeared on an allowlisted source, so the cited figures remain unchanged pending a citable update. Re-checked 9 August 2026: ReliefWeb's Pakistan country page shows no OCHA 'Monsoon Situation Update - 2' or newer edition beyond Situation Update - 1 (3 August 2026); the cited figures (126 deaths, 416 injuries) remain unchanged. Non-allowlisted NDMA-sourced press reports a higher toll (151 deaths, 448 injured as of 8 August) that has not yet appeared on an allowlisted source. Re-checked 11 August 2026: direct fetch of reliefweb.int/country/pak again returned HTTP 403; a targeted web search found no OCHA 'Monsoon Situation Update - 2' or any newer allowlisted report, only continued non-allowlisted Pakistani press coverage (Pakistan Today, Daily Times) citing NDMA for a toll around 151 deaths as of 8 August, which still has not been corroborated on an allowlisted source. The cited figures (126 deaths, 416 injuries, as of the 3 August OCHA update) remain the freshest citable total and are unchanged. Re-checked 12 August 2026: OCHA's 'Pakistan: 2026 Monsoon Situation Update - 2' (as of 10 August 2026) records a nationwide toll of 153 deaths and 457 injuries, with 1,339 houses damaged and 576 livestock lost, up from the prior 126 deaths/416 injuries (3 August). Pakistan's NDMA Daily Situation Report No. 47 (11 August 2026) gives the most current government figures: 155 deaths, 460 injuries, 1,341 houses damaged and 580 livestock lost, cumulative since 26 June 2026. The two sources are closely aligned (one day apart) and both corroborate the previously-uncorroborated Pakistani press figures (~151 deaths, 8 August) that had been withheld pending an allowlisted citation. NDMA's Flood Forecasting Division bulletin (11 August 2026) reports all major rivers at Below-Low or Low flood severity, with the Ravi and Chenab possibly reaching Low Flood Level again over the 12-18 August outlook. NDMA's Daily Situation Report No. 49 (13 August 2026) shows the death toll unchanged at 155 while injuries rose to 468 (+8) and cumulative house damage to 1,345 (+4), all in Rajanpur, Punjab, in the latest 24-hour window; NDMA continues logging new casualties and damage daily, and the Pakistan Meteorological Department forecasts a fresh rain spell for 13-15 August. Re-checked 14 August 2026: NDMA's sitrep archive shows Daily Situation Report No. 49 (13 August 2026) as still the latest edition; no newer OCHA Monsoon Situation Update was found. Figures (155 deaths, 468 injured) remain unchanged.
